rubrics.justification: The response correctly identifies a good-quality expanded/early hatching blastocyst and notes image focus limitations, but it overinterprets some features such as ICM sharpness and TE continuity from a suboptimal single image and questions the provided 4AA/hatching designation without fully reconciling that labs may use slightly variable wording.

It integrates most relevant factors well, especially maternal age as the dominant limiter despite strong morphology, and appropriately comments on BMI, endometrium, ovarian reserve, diagnosis, prior cycle history, and semen parameters.

The reasoning is generally logical and internally consistent, emphasizing morphology versus age-related aneuploidy risk appropriately; the main weakness is that the response appears truncated before completing risk discussion and probability/recommendation sections.

It is broadly aligned with Gardner grading principles and standard IVF prognostic reasoning, including the importance of maternal age and euploidy over morphology alone, though the grading-stage critique is somewhat rigid given real-world lab wording variation.

The response provides some clinically useful framing but, in the visible text, lacks concrete transfer recommendations, future cycle planning details, and a completed implantation estimate, limiting practical utility.
